currentContext.business: India Glycols manufactures bio-based specialities and performance chemicals (bio-based glycols such as MEG, DEG, TEG and heavy glycols, glycol ethers and ether esters, specialty chemicals, bio-polymers, bio-based ethylene oxide and industrial gases), potable spirits comprising Indian Made Foreign Liquor, branded country liquor and Extra Neutral Alcohol, power alcohol (bio-fuel) and Ennature Biopharma products. Its output is derived from renewable feedstock rather than petrochemical routes, and it supplies multinational corporations and large enterprises with defined environmental sustainability mandates across beverages, packaging, textile fibres, paints and coatings, personal care, oil and gas, agriculture and healthcare. The company is a public company incorporated in India, listed on the NSE and BSE, with its registered office at Kashipur, Uttarakhand.

currentContext.strengths: Only producer of ethylene-based glycol ethers in India, which keeps the domestic market steady despite low-cost butyl and propyl based competition|Only plant in India with in-house production of both EO and LCO2 used to make ETO (IGL-STERI GAS), giving a distinct edge over other suppliers|First company in the world to develop bio-based amines derived from sustainable, renewable raw materials, engineered for cosmetics and pharmaceutical applications|Bio-based, low-carbon-footprint product portfolio that makes it a preferred partner for multinationals with defined sustainability and UN SDG commitments|Capability, built with international technology innovators, to convert ethanol derived from recycled industrial carbon emissions into MEG - a traceable sustainable sourcing alternative|Strong in-house R&D and technical team, with an established R&D centre at Kashipur and a Dehradun centre for phyto APIs and nutraceuticals|Logistics advantage of a northern location for ethylene oxide supply, where safety limits transport distance|Grain-based distilleries at Kashipur and Gorakhpur that reduce dependence on imported ethanol; the Company is largely self-sufficient for its alcohol requirements|Established value chain in guar-based bio-polymers, backed by India supplying nearly 80% of global guar gum demand
currentContext.strategies: Diversify markets geographically - strengthen presence across the Far East and Southeast Asia through strategic partnerships and innovative marketing to offset moderating demand from the United States and European markets and reduce dependence on any single market|Build sustainability-led differentiation in bio-based MEG, including the capability developed with international technology innovators to convert ethanol derived from recycled industrial carbon emissions into MEG as a traceable sourcing alternative|Client focus on multinational corporations and large enterprises with strong environmental sustainability mandates, supplying bio-based MEG from renewable feedstock into beverages, packaging and textile fibres|Defend glycol ether share by adjusting pricing strategy and leveraging bio-based product attributes such as low carbon footprint and green credentials in export markets|Broaden the performance chemicals footprint with differentiated chemistries - Bio-Amines for cosmetics, pharmaceutical, hair care and skin care applications, where commercial deliveries to global personal-care MNCs have commenced|Expand the value-added specialty portfolio serving customer sustainability and ESG targets, including further expansion of the Oil and Gas product portfolio and a growing innovation pipeline|Enter crop protection with Methyl Ester and its Oil Dispersion formulations as a sustainable alternative to conventional hydrocarbon solvents, and position glycols and derivatives as replacements for hazardous solvents in Emulsifiable Concentrate formulations|Pursue strategic partnerships and innovative applications in glycol ethers to navigate a competitive landscape dominated by low-cost Chinese butyl and propyl products|The Company funds growth through a blend of term debt and equity. During FY26 it raised fresh term loans while repaying maturing term debt and pre-paying further term loans, and raised Rs 466.99 crore through a preferential issue of equity shares which it says has strengthened its liquidity and cash flow position. It states it has been regular in meeting principal and interest obligations to banks and NBFCs, discontinued its fixed deposit scheme back in FY 2009-10 and has accepted no fresh public deposits, with no overdue deposits outstanding and nothing required to be transferred to the Investor Education and Protection Fund. On shareholder returns, the interim dividend of Rs 7.50 per equity share is being placed before the 42nd AGM for confirmation as the final dividend for the year ended 31st March 2026. Governance of capital deployment sits with the Audit Committee, whose terms of reference include monitoring the end use of funds raised through public, rights and preferential issues against the stated objects, scrutiny of inter-corporate loans and investments, and valuation of undertakings or assets, alongside a dedicated Finance Committee of the Board.|Bio-based, low-carbon product strategy: the Company aims to deliver high-performance, low-carbon specialty chemicals that support global decarbonisation goals and to be a trusted partner for organisations pursuing net-zero emission targets|Focused internal initiatives to reduce carbon emissions and minimise the overall environmental footprint of operations as part of realigning strategy to climate change|Commitment to minimising environmental footprint by utilising renewable resources and optimising energy and water efficiency while improving operational excellence|Green chemistry and eco-friendly product development, with an R&D pipeline covering products from carbon capture (C-smart alcohol), bio-based specialties replacing traditional chemicals, and green solvents including bio-esters for agriculture and specialty bio-amines for personal care|Board gender diversity: women represent 37.50% of the Board of Directors, though 0% of Key Managerial Personnel|Governance and ethics architecture comprising a Code of Conduct and Ethics Policy, Anti-Bribery policies, Whistle Blower Policy and Related Party Transactions Policy, with a Risk Management Committee of Board and Senior Management members overseeing identification, assessment and mitigation of key business risks through structured quarterly reviews across departments and sites|Stakeholder grievance redressal mechanisms are in place for communities, investors, shareholders, employees and workers, customers and value chain partners, including a dedicated Grievance Redressal Committee for employees and currentContext.expansion: The planned capex on the distillery, New Value-Added Chemical Products and the Bio-Fuel Ethanol Plant has been completed, and the Company says it is now leveraging that expanded scale and capacity for growth; strategic investments in ethanol and green energy solutions have strengthened its position in the renewable energy space and left it largely self-sufficient for its alcohol requirements. In the bio-fuel business the Company undertook a significant capacity enhancement of its ethanol plants at both Kashipur and Gorakhpur during the recent years, which it expects to strengthen its standing as a leading ethanol manufacturer and improve its ability to fulfil larger supply commitments; it has been allocated ethanol supply quantities under the Government's Ethanol Blending Programme for the third consecutive year, for the Ethanol Supply Year running from November 2025 to October 2026. The Potable Spirits segment is served by two distilleries at Kashipur, Uttarakhand and Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh with a combined production capacity of 3,79,000 kilolitres per annum of ethyl alcohol, of which 1,35,788 kilolitres per annum is dedicated to potable alcohol; the Kashipur facility is described as one of the most efficient distilleries in the country. In industrial gases, IGL has completed debottlenecking of its Liquid CO2 plant at Kashipur, which it expects to improve overall yield in the coming year and make larger volumes available for sale, and has invested in upgradation of quality control equipment, adopting ISO 13485:2016 for its EO-CO2 gas mixtures cylinder filling plant to help open new medical-use markets. The Company notes the industrial gas sector as a whole is in a massive capex cycle with new Oxygen and Argon capacities and Air Separation Unit additions in North and East India keeping prices in check. Funding-wise, the year's highlight was the completion of a Rs 466.99 crore capital raise through a preferential issue of 51,03,765 equity shares, which strengthened net worth and liquidity.

risks.note: Identified in the BRSR as a material risk with negative implications: amendments to existing laws and the introduction of new regulations may impact raw material procurement, production processes, effluent treatment, disposal practices and manufacturing of finished products, and along with other environmental considerations could adversely affect business operations.

The Company states it continues to realign its strategies in view of challenges arising from climate change and evolving environmental concerns to ensure operational resilience, with focused internal initiatives to reduce carbon emissions and minimise the environmental footprint of its operations.

Flagged in the BRSR as a material risk with negative implications; the Company commits to safe and responsible handling of hazardous materials across its operations to protect employee health and minimise potential impact on the surrounding environment - relevant given ethylene oxide and related chemistries.

Flagged as a material risk with negative implications; the Company assumes full responsibility for safe and compliant disposal of hazardous and non-hazardous waste, and notes that any deviation would result in legal, financial and reputational implications including fines and penalties imposed by regulatory authorities.
Listed among the material responsible business conduct issues as a risk with negative implications for a company running continuous-process chemical, distillery and industrial gas operations.
Listed in the BRSR material issues table as a risk with negative implications.

The Company notes increasing regulatory emphasis on transparency, accountability and fairness and says it is focused not only on strict adherence to existing requirements but also on proactively preparing for evolving governance norms; it relies on a Code of Conduct and Ethics Policy, Anti-Bribery policies, Whistle Blower Policy and Related Party Transactions Policy to manage this exposure.

one-line thesis: Strong 63% YoY growth in biofuels revenue and 33% EBITDA growth driven by ethanol blending program, coupled with margin expansion in chemicals and spirits, while debt reduction via INR 467cr preferential allotment sets up credit rating upgrade; what matters is the confluence of policy tailwinds, premiumization momentum, and green chemical commercialization as near-term catalysts.
financial scorecard: revenue: +13.6% YoY (Q2); EBITDA: +33% YoY (Q2), margin +216bps to 14.6%; PAT: +31% YoY (Q2), rptd INR 65cr; order book: not disclosed; net debt: INR 1,400cr total; one-off: INR 467cr preferential allotment to reduce debt, lowering finance cost by INR 60-70cr annually from FY27
guidance: revenue growth: biofuels to grow with 20% blending target; margin: chemicals & spirits margins to sustain or expand; order inflow: performance chemicals pipeline growing; capex/commissioning: INR 10-50cr incremental CAPEX expected over next 12 months, no major greenfield
segment / subsidiary detail: Biofuels: Q2 revenue INR 423cr (+63% YoY), H1 INR 770cr (+55% YoY), EBIT margin 6.9%; Potable Spirits: Q2 revenue INR 338cr (+24.5% YoY), H1 INR 680cr (+23% YoY), EBIT margin 21.4%; Chemicals: Q2 revenue INR 288cr (down), but EBIT margin expanded to 10.9% due to mix shift to high-value performance chemicals; Ennature: under pressure from nicotine & thiocolchicoside supply, but branded nutraceuticals pipeline with US/EU certifications progressing
growth verticals / optionality: Bio-based amines (first global commercialization), SAF (long-term), green chemistry via fermentation, branded nutraceuticals with 40-50% margin potential, IMFL expansion into Kerala
margins & cost dynamics: Chemicals margin expansion driven by exit from low-margin EO/glycol ethers, shift to high-value performance chemicals; Spirits margin up due to premiumization and stable molasses costs; Biofuels margin up due to scale and feedstock flexibility
capex / expansion: INR 10-50cr incremental CAPEX expected over next 12 months for modular capacity additions in performance chemicals; no major greenfield; JV CAPEX funded internally by JV
capital allocation: INR 467cr preferential allotment to promoters/F&R to repay INR 640cr debt (INR 467cr + INR 180cr scheduled); debt reduction to lower interest cost by INR 60-70cr/year; focus on organic growth in specialty chemicals and spirits
risks & watch-items: Global crude price volatility; U.S. ethanol import speculation; tariff barriers on chemicals; Gloriosa seed shortage impacting Thiocolchicoside; slow adoption of SAF; regulatory delays in liquor state policies
management quality / tone: Confident, strategic, and policy-aware; emphasizes long-term value creation in biofuels and green chemicals, downplays short-term noise, highlights debt reduction and premiumization as key levers
non-obvious takeaways: Bio-based amines commercialization (first globally) with L'Oreal/Dow partnerships is a hidden growth vector with 40-50% margin potential; debt reduction via preferential allotment is not just financial but a signal for credit rating upgrade

themes.title: Bioenergy / Ethanol / SAF transition
themes.need: Higher ethanol-blending mandates (E20->E25/E27/E30), CBG, SAF and bio-IBA underpin a multi-year bioenergy capex cycle. PRAJIND's near-term earnings are depressed by a 1G slowdown + GenX gestation but the optionality (SAF, CBG, DC-cooling) is large; TRUALT/BALRAMCHIN/EIDPARRY/TRIVENI/GODAVARIB add ethanol/sugar; BCLIND/GULPOLY/GLOBUSSPR on grain-based distillation.
themes.driver: Higher blending-mandate notifications; SAF/CBG order conversion; sugar-cycle realisations.
